narrative:
The model estimated a 37% probability that you would be a bad credit risk. In practical terms, about one in three applicants with a similar profile would struggle to repay, and that risk was above the bank’s approval cut-off, so your application was denied.

The most important reason was your checking-account status. Your account is currently negative, which is uncommon among approved applicants: most have no negative balance, while only 12.6% are in the same negative range as you. This was the strongest factor pushing the decision toward bad credit. Your credit purpose and requested duration worked in your favour. A radio/TV loan is common among approved applicants, at 35%, and a 12-month term is shorter than the approved average of about 19 months, so both helped push toward good credit. They were not enough to outweigh the checking-account concern.

Your next step should be to stabilise your checking account: bring it out of negative balance and show a consistent positive balance without overdrafts. Ask the lender whether updated account statements or a guarantor could be considered. Because a shorter term and a clear purpose already helped your profile, keep your next request modest and well documented, and reapply once your account history is stronger.
